# Phase One — Track Palace Possibility

The Awtsmoos renews every sound before row and toolbar can divide;
Awtsmoos.com lets the archive become one clean river where hidden runtime styles no longer hide.

## Proven starting reality

- `ui/browser/tracks.js` actively imports and invokes `ensureTrackStyles()`.
- `tracks/styles.js` injects a compressed `<style>` string into the document.
- The runtime string owns toolbar, row, checkbox, command, state, and mobile rules.
- It uses generic `:focus`, hover, and disabled states but lacks a complete explicit active/reduced-motion contract.
- Track JS files are Git-clean before this wave.
- Several live track modules use two-space indentation and `innerHTML` even though safe DOM is practical.
- Rebbe search is 7/7 test-green and the live Rebbe route returns HTTP 200 on port 8913.

## Possibility field

- Move all track styling into static route-local CSS imported by `runtime-ui.css`.
- Make `ensureTrackStyles()` a compatibility no-op or remove its active call while preserving export compatibility.
- Split toolbar, row, checkbox, command, and interaction CSS by responsibility.
- Give every visible command a >=44px touch target.
- Replace generic focus with `:focus-visible`.
- Add explicit hover, active, disabled, saved, and reduced-motion behavior.
- Preserve event toolbar command vocabulary exactly.
- Preserve row command vocabulary exactly.
- Replace `innerHTML` in track rows, toolbar copy, selection checkbox, and cache mark with DOM construction/textContent.
- Convert internal construction into class-based factories/controllers while preserving old public function exports.
- Replace `onclick` assignments with `addEventListener` where touched.
- Use `replaceChildren()` instead of `innerHTML = ''` for the track list.
- Keep every source file <=120 lines without compressed functions.
- Add regression contracts for static style ownership, callback vocabulary, safe DOM, interaction states, and mobile layout.
